ai_decision.authorship: Current Work AI after actual source/ket/population/quality reading. No runtime LLM, prewritten optimizer or independently reviewed science claimed.
ai_decision.falsifier: Pe>=1e-4 fails the bounded return-pulse forecast; no decrease also challenges the selected control phase/model mapping. Numerical failure stops with raw evidence, not phase correction or retry.
ai_decision.limits: Source levels/dipole are finite-basis RHF/TDA response parameters. Two-state truncation, continuum, omitted couplings, ionization, nuclei and real experimental preparation remain unqualified. No exact molecular dynamics or novel physics claim.
ai_decision.physical_question: Can phase control of a second pulse reverse population transfer in the same computed two-state effective model, using its ACTUALLY saved coherent state rather than preparing a new ground state?
ai_decision.prediction: After one further400atomic-time-unit pulse, Pe(t=800)<1e-4 and below Pe(t=400), while norm error<1e-7 and tolerance-population difference<1e-6. Counterrotating terms may leave a small residual; no exact zero or full molecular return claimed.
ai_decision.resource_reason: Second and last approved Job reuses the exact source model and saved ket; one evolution plus one declared tighter-tolerance replica, no new electronic solve or scan.
ai_decision.scalar_control_derivation: Transform b/a into the resonant interaction picture using computed gap and current time400. Set global carrier phase=-pi/2-arg(b_I/a), convert to local pulse phase by adding gap*t0 and wrap to[-pi,pi]. Choose E2=4*atan2(|b|,|a|)/(mu_z*400) from observed rotation angle and sin² pulse area. These are RWA control-design approximations only; actual propagation retains full cosine and existing QuTiP settings.
ai_decision.stop_after: Read second actual observation, compare, submit B-Chat and STOP. No third run or automatic rerun.
ai_decision.why_now: First coherent excitation is finite and well resolved against integrator error, and saved complex phase is available. A phase-sensitive continuation tests a newly opened degree of freedom; merely doubling a prepared-state pulse would not test coherent state continuity as directly.
